name: lateral line system
definition: A sensory system on the surface of the fish, consisting of small sensory patches (neuromasts) distributed in discrete lines over the body surface. The lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance. (See Anatomical Atlas entry for lateral line by T. Whitfield.)

name: pancreas
definition: The pancreas is an organ composed of endocrine and exocrine glandular tissue that produce hormones and digestive enzymes. Unlike in other studied vertebrates the pancreas in zebrafish develops from two buds, one anterior and one posterior. In adult fish the main pancreas is located on the right side attached to the lateral aspect of the intestine by the pancreatic duct. Typically, one large islet and 3-6 smaller islets occupy the main pancreas. The tail of the pancreas is embedded with single beta cells or clusters of small islets and extends caudally along the right side of the intestine.
overrideNote: Handoff pancreatic_buds_pancreas: the dorsal and ventral pancreatic buds hand off to the pancreas over 48 to 60 hpf (D9); the window start equals the ZFA start (Long-pec, 48 hpf). DM-36: axis clamp at 4320 hpf.

name: epidermis

overrideNote: DM-36: the axis end is a clamp; ZFA carries the term to the adult stage. The periderm ZFA:0001185 is its own record from 10 to 168 hpf (review DR-08; spec 3.5.3); the whole-organism skin tube (DM-31) draws the surface and this node is the tree row for the skin layers, scales and barbels.

events.text: ZFIN start stage Prim-5; epidermis about 4 um, two layers.
stratification begins at 5.4 to 6 mm SL (head) and 6.7 mm SL (dorsal trunk), about 25 dpf.
four to six cell layers by 8.6 mm SL.

sizes.note: 20 um head, 40 to 60 um dorsal trunk, 10 um ventral abdomen

name: pharyngeal arch
definition: One of a series of paired bony or cartilaginous arches that develop along the lateral walls of the foregut. The pharyngeal arches have developmental contributions from endoderm, mesoderm, and neural crest cells and are separated by anterior lateral endoderm out-pockets known as pharyngeal pouches. There are seven pharyngeal arches.
overrideNote: DM-36: the axis end is a clamp; ZFA carries the term to the adult stage. Group node of the three arch records (arch 1, arch 2, arches 3-7); D5 places the pharyngeal arch in the skeletal system with alsoIn respiratory (review DR-01).

name: lepidotrichium
definition: Dermal bone that is rod-like, formed and usually contained in a fin membrane, and jointed to or adjacent to distal radials. They are bilaterally paired.  Lepidotrichia are formed from paired hemitrichia surrounding actinotrichia. There are usually two more lepidotrichia than distal radials.
overrideNote: ZFIN start stage Unknown (DM-19): the first lepidotrichia are the caudal fin rays at 4.9 mm SL (280 hpf on the growth table; Parichy et al. 2009). DM-36: axis clamp at 4320 hpf. Group node (review DR-07): the rays are drawn by the rays parameter of each fin's finSheet (count, lengthFraction, thicknessMm on the pectoral, pelvic, dorsal, anal and caudal fin records) and carry the fin material; this record is the card and tree row for the fin rays. A per-fin derived ray part in the bone colour is a builder request.

events.text: First caudal fin rays at 4.9 to 5.1 mm SL.
Anal fin rays at 6.1 to 6.4 mm SL; dorsal fin rays at 6.4 to 6.6 mm SL.
Pelvic fin rays at 8.5 to 8.7 mm SL (D8: 8.6 mm SL).
Ray segment addition proceeds linearly through about 11 mm SL.

sizes.note: caudal plus anal plus dorsal rays
all fins; caudal about 19 principal rays, anal about 15, dorsal about 10, pectoral 10 to 12, pelvic 7

name: periderm
definition: The outermost epidermal layer covering the fish at embryonic stages; derived from the EVL and thought to eventually be replaced by the superficial stratum of the epidermis. Sometimes used synonymously with EVL.
overrideNote: ZFA ends the periderm at 26+ somites (24 hpf), when the epidermis term starts; the model keeps the record to 168 hpf with a 24 h fade because a peridermal layer persists on the larva for days (research 03a; spec 3.5.3). Group node (review DR-08): the whole-organism skin tube (DM-31) draws the 2 to 3 um layer as the surface; this record is the card and tree row.

events.text: EVL forms as the outermost blastoderm monolayer (ZFIN start 30%-epiboly for EVL).
ZFIN start stage Bud for periderm.
ZFIN end stage 26+ somites; the superficial stratum of the epidermis replaces it.
Model end: a peridermal layer persists on the larva for days; the record ends with the yolk at 168 hpf (research 03a).

sizes.note: outer of the two epidermal layers
the two-layer epidermis is about 4 um thick at 24 hpf; the periderm is its outer layer

events.text: Segments 4 to 7 deform simultaneously into chevrons.
Posterior segments deform sequentially into chevrons, about 2 h each.
